source_text:
Synthetic validation nurse note. No real patient data.

The patient has confirmed type 2 diabetes and is acutely unwell at the current assessment. The treating physician's signed note explicitly documents metabolically unstable diabetes after reviewing current observations and laboratory results; this is a documented clinical assessment rather than a diagnosis inferred by the nurse from thirst alone. The patient describes nausea and fluctuating blur, and the planned work assessment has been interrupted for clinical care.

The GP's separate current summary records that persistent blood pressure remains 182/108 mmHg after repeated measurements. A measurement copied from an older employment form is lower, but the clinician identifies the repeated current values as persistent, and the nurse keeps the older form separate rather than averaging different time periods.

The driver cannot provide a reliable account of the latest diabetes medication change or a complete glucose log, and the visual symptoms have not received an independent specialist assessment. Those missing details remain unresolved even though current metabolic instability and persistent blood pressure are explicitly documented by the treating clinicians.
